**Four of the eight filings qualify: Walmart, Berkshire Hathaway, Pfizer and Boeing.**

| Filing | Named company acquired | Evidence that the acquisition closed during fiscal 2025 |
|---|---|---|
| **Walmart fiscal 2025 Form 10-K** | **VIZIO Holding Corp.** | States that “in December 2024, the Walmart U.S. segment completed the acquisition of VIZIO Holding Corp.” for $1.9 billion in net cash consideration—within the fiscal year ended January 31, 2025. *WMT_2025_10K.pdf*, p. 34. |
| **Berkshire Hathaway 2025 Form 10-K** | **Bell Laboratories, LLC** | Explicitly states: “Berkshire acquired Bell Laboratories, LLC … on July 31, 2025.” This is the Wisconsin rodent-control-products company. *BRK_2025_10K.pdf*, printed p. K-15 (PDF p. 17). |
| **Pfizer 2025 Form 10-K** | **Metsera** | Note 2 states: “On November 13, 2025, we acquired Metsera,” describing the cash-per-share purchase plus contingent value rights. *PFE_2025_10K.pdf*, printed p. 64 (PDF p. 73). |
| **Boeing 2025 Form 10-K** | **Spirit AeroSystems Holdings, Inc.** | Note 2 states that Boeing completed the acquisition on **December 8, 2025**, becoming the ultimate parent of Spirit and its subsidiaries. This was a company acquisition, notwithstanding Spirit’s concurrent divestiture of certain operations to Airbus. *BA_2025_10K.pdf*, printed pp. 70–71 (PDF pp. 74–75). |

**The other four do not meet your filing-based test:**

- **NVIDIA:** Reports acquisitions and shares issued to employees of acquired companies, but **does not name those acquired companies**. Its named Arm transaction was terminated, not completed. *NVDA_2025_10K.pdf*, pp. 34, 62 and 65.
- **Apple:** Does **not report a named, completed whole-company acquisition** during fiscal 2025 in this filing.
- **JPMorgan Chase:** The First Republic transaction described in the filing occurred on **May 1, 2023**, involved certain assets and liabilities, and its 2025 purchase-price settlement was not a new acquisition. The CIFM acquisition gain also relates to 2023. *JPM_2025_10K.pdf*, printed pp. 221 and 312 (PDF pp. 223 and 314).
- **ExxonMobil:** Its 2025 Superior Graphite transaction is expressly an acquisition of **“key technology and assets,”** not the company. Pioneer and Denbury were acquired in **2024 and 2023**, respectively. *XOM_2025_10K.pdf*, printed pp. 54 and 112–113 (PDF pp. 56 and 114–115).

Berkshire’s **OxyChem** acquisition is excluded because it closed on **January 2, 2026**, after fiscal 2025 ended.

**Three of the eight filings identify a collective group as the chief operating decision maker (CODM):**

| Company | Group identified as the CODM | Filing reference |
|---|---|---|
| **JPMorgan Chase** | **Operating Committee**, “whose members act collectively as the Firm’s CODM.” | 2024 Form 10-K, Note 32, printed p. 313 (PDF p. 315). |
| **Berkshire Hathaway** | No separate group name is given. It consists of the **Chairman and Chief Executive Officer**, the **Vice Chairman of Insurance Operations**, and the **Vice Chairman of Non-Insurance Operations**. The filing states that this group is ultimately responsible for significant capital-allocation decisions and evaluating operating performance. | 2024 Form 10-K, Note 26, printed p. K-108 (PDF p. 110). |
| **ExxonMobil** | **Management Committee (MC)**. The filing explicitly says its members are considered “collectively, and not in their individual capacity” to be the CODM. It comprises the **CEO, CFO, and two Senior Vice Presidents serving as contact executives overseeing the Upstream and Product Solutions businesses**. | 2024 Form 10-K, Note 18, printed p. 108 (PDF p. 110). |

The specified filings of **NVIDIA, Apple, Walmart, Pfizer, and Boeing do not identify a collective executive group as CODM**. NVIDIA, Pfizer, and Boeing expressly identify an individual executive; Apple’s and Walmart’s cited segment notes refer to the CODM without identifying a collective group.

**Three of the eight filings qualify: NVIDIA, Apple, and JPMorgan Chase.** Counting distinct directors or officers—not plans or shares—the results are:

| Fiscal 2024 filing | Number of people | People named and adoption dates | Source |
|---|---:|---|---|
| **NVIDIA** — year ended January 28, 2024 | **1** | **John O. Dabiri**, director — December 18, 2023 | Item 9B, p. 45 |
| **Apple** — year ended September 28, 2024 | **2** | **Deirdre O’Brien**, SVP, Retail — August 27, 2024; **Jeff Williams**, COO — August 29, 2024 | Item 9B, printed p. 52 (PDF p. 55) |
| **JPMorgan Chase** — year ended December 31, 2024 | **5** | **Lori Beer** — November 15; **James Dimon** — November 7; **Robin Leopold** — November 4; **Jennifer Piepszak** — October 30; **Troy Rohrbaugh** — November 15, all in 2024 | Item 9B, printed p. 41 (PDF p. 43) |

Each of these disclosures expressly identifies the arrangements as intended to satisfy the affirmative defense of **Rule 10b5-1(c)**.

The other five filings explicitly report **no qualifying director/officer adoptions during the final fiscal quarter**:

- **Walmart:** Item 9B, p. 81.
- **Berkshire Hathaway:** Item 9B, p. K-117 (PDF p. 119).
- **Pfizer:** Item 9B, printed p. 109 (PDF p. 121).
- **ExxonMobil:** Item 9B, printed p. 29 (PDF p. 31).
- **Boeing:** Item 9B, printed p. 127 (PDF p. 131).

Company share-repurchase arrangements are excluded from these counts.

Boeing’s 2022 Form 10-K reports the following capitalized precontract costs as of **December 31, 2022**, all in **millions of dollars**:

| Amount | What it relates to |
|---:|---|
| **$794 million** | Total capitalized precontract costs included in inventories. Note 7 identifies KC-46A Tanker, Commercial Crew, and T-7 Production Options among the related programs. |
| **Approximately $209 million** | **KC-46A Tanker** costs related to unexercised future production lots. |
| **Approximately $56 million** | **T-7A Red Hawk** costs related to future production lots. |
| **Approximately $180 million** | **Commercial Crew (CST-100 Starliner)** costs related to unauthorized future missions. |

The three specifically disclosed program amounts are **not a complete reconciliation** of the $794 million total.

**Sources:** Note 7, printed p. 76 (PDF p. 80); Note 13, printed pp. 87–88 (PDF pp. 91–92), *BA_2022_10K.pdf*.

**Three filings qualify: Apple, JPMorgan Chase and ExxonMobil.** Their reported fiscal-2021 year-end commercial paper balances were:

| Company | Fiscal year-end | Commercial paper outstanding | Filing evidence |
|---|---|---:|---|
| **Apple** | September 25, 2021 | **$6.0 billion** | Note 7, “Debt—Commercial Paper and Repurchase Agreements,” states that Apple had $6.0 billion outstanding and uses the proceeds for general corporate purposes, including dividends and share repurchases. *2021 Form 10-K*, p. 44 (PDF p. 47). |
| **JPMorgan Chase** | December 31, 2021 | **$15,108 million** | “Sources of funds (excluding deposits)” reports this amount in the **year-end 2021** column, separately from the $12,285 million annual average. Commercial paper is classified as short-term unsecured funding; conduit obligations appear separately and are excluded here. *2021 Form 10-K*, p. 102 (PDF p. 104). |
| **ExxonMobil** | December 31, 2021 | **$1,608 million** | Note 6, “Additional Working Capital Information,” lists commercial paper of $1,608 million under “Notes and loans payable.” *2021 Form 10-K*, p. 82 (PDF p. 84). |

**The other three filings do not report a qualifying positive year-end commercial paper balance:**

- **Pfizer:** Note 7C explicitly reports **“—” (zero)** commercial paper at December 31, 2021, versus $556 million in 2020. Printed p. 79 (PDF p. 85).
- **Berkshire Hathaway:** Note 18 reports subsidiary short-term borrowings and mentions unused commercial paper capacity, but **does not identify a positive commercial paper balance outstanding**. The broader short-term borrowing totals should not be treated as commercial paper amounts. Printed pp. K-99–K-100 (PDF pp. 101–102).
- **Boeing:** Note 15’s year-end debt disclosures **do not report commercial paper outstanding**. Printed pp. 98–99 (PDF pp. 101–102).

Thus, the qualifying amounts are **Apple: $6.0 billion; JPMorgan Chase: $15,108 million; ExxonMobil: $1,608 million**.

**Berkshire Hathaway and ExxonMobil** are the two filings that disclose the requested cumulative year-end excess.

| Company | Excess at December 31, 2021 (US$ billions) | Disclosure and source |
|---|---:|---|
| **Berkshire Hathaway** | **Approximately 1.9** | “The excess of current or replacement costs over costs determined under LIFO was approximately $1.9 billion.” Note 1(k), *Inventories*, printed p. K-77 (PDF p. 79). |
| **ExxonMobil** | **Estimated 14.0** | “The aggregate replacement cost of inventories was estimated to exceed their LIFO carrying values by $14.0 billion.” Note 3, *Miscellaneous Financial Information*, printed p. 80 (PDF p. 82). |

The other four filings do **not** disclose such a year-end LIFO excess:
- **Apple:** inventories use FIFO—Note 1, printed p. 35.
- **JPMorgan Chase:** no corresponding LIFO excess disclosure; its physical-commodity inventory valuation is discussed in Note 2, printed p. 175.
- **Pfizer:** inventories use average actual cost—Note 1J, printed p. 61.
- **Boeing:** its inventory policies and Note 7 do not report a LIFO excess—printed pp. 70–71 and 85.

These are **cumulative balances at year-end**, not annual changes or LIFO-related effects on earnings.

**Apple and Pfizer** disclose the total remaining transition-tax payments in their fiscal 2021 Form 10-Ks. The other four filings do not separately state that remaining amount.

| Company | Remaining amount disclosed? | Total still to be paid (US$ billions) | Filing evidence |
|---|---|---:|---|
| **Apple** | **Yes** | **24.6** | “Deemed Repatriation Tax Payable” states that the balance at September 25, 2021 was **$24.6 billion**, none payable within 12 months. *2021 Form 10-K, printed p. 25 (PDF p. 28).* |
| JPMorgan Chase | No | Not separately stated | Its 2021 filing does not separately quantify the remaining transition-tax obligation. |
| Berkshire Hathaway | No | Not separately stated | Its 2021 filing does not separately quantify the remaining transition-tax obligation. |
| **Pfizer** | **Yes** | **8.3** | “Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements, Contractual, and Other Obligations” states that estimated future TCJA repatriation-tax payments after December 31, 2021 **total $8.3 billion**. *2021 Form 10-K, printed p. 47 (PDF p. 53).* |
| ExxonMobil | No | Not separately stated | Its 2021 filing does not separately quantify the remaining transition-tax obligation. |
| Boeing | No | Not separately stated | Its income-tax note mentions the TCJA one-time repatriation tax but does not give the remaining payable. |

For Pfizer, **$8.3 billion is the explicitly reported total**, rather than its original estimated $15 billion liability or the $750 million expected within the next twelve months. “Not separately stated” does **not** mean zero.

**Five of the eight filings report qualifying share repurchases during fiscal 2025:** NVIDIA, Apple, Walmart, JPMorgan Chase and ExxonMobil.

| Company | Fiscal year ended | Full-year shares repurchased (millions, as stated) | Filing reference |
|---|---|---:|---|
| NVIDIA | January 26, 2025 | **310** | Item 5, “Issuer Purchases of Equity Securities,” p. 33 |
| Apple | September 27, 2025 | **402** | Note 10, “Shareholders’ Equity—Share Repurchase Program,” p. 44 (PDF p. 47) |
| Walmart | January 31, 2025 | **61.9** | Note 3, “Shareholders’ Equity—Share Repurchase Program,” p. 67; reported on a settlement-date basis |
| JPMorgan Chase | December 31, 2025 | **114.4** | MD&A, “Capital actions—Common stock repurchases,” p. 97 (PDF p. 99) |
| ExxonMobil | December 31, 2025 | **180.1** | MD&A, “Cash Flow from Financing Activities—2025,” p. 60 (PDF p. 62) |

**The other three do not qualify:**

- **Berkshire Hathaway:** expressly states, “There were no share repurchases in 2025.” — “Financial Condition,” p. K-55 (PDF p. 57).
- **Pfizer:** states that it did not purchase common shares under its publicly announced share-purchase plan in any of the periods presented. — Note 12, “Equity—Common Stock Purchases,” p. 89 (PDF p. 101).
- **Boeing:** states that its open-market common-stock repurchase program was terminated in March 2020. Its reported 2025 employee tax-withholding share transfers are excluded under your criteria. — Item 5, p. 23, and MD&A, p. 43 (PDF pp. 25 and 45).

The totals above use the filings’ stated **million-share figures**, rather than converting more precise share counts, and exclude employee tax withholding, plan-trustee purchases and post-year-end repurchases.

**Two of the eight filings report qualifying preferred-stock issuances during fiscal 2024: JPMorgan Chase and Boeing.**

| Filing | Issuance date | What was issued |
|---|---|---|
| **JPMorgan Chase — 2024 Form 10-K** | **March 12, 2024** | **$2.5 billion of fixed-rate reset non-cumulative preferred stock, Series NN.** Note 21 explicitly reports the issuance; its accompanying table shows 250,000 preferred shares represented by depositary shares. (Note 21, printed pp. 291–292; PDF pp. 293–294.) |
| **Boeing — 2024 Form 10-K** | **October 31, 2024** | **115,000,000 depositary shares representing 5,750,000 shares of 6.00% Series A Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock.** (Note 19, “Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock,” printed p. 106; PDF p. 110.) |

The other six filings—**NVIDIA, Apple, Walmart, Berkshire Hathaway, Pfizer and ExxonMobil**—do **not** report issuing new shares of their own preferred stock during the specified fiscal years.

JPMorgan’s filing also discloses a **February 4, 2025** Series OO issuance, but that is **outside fiscal 2024** and is therefore excluded.

**Only Pfizer and Walmart** disclose an amount meeting your criteria in their fiscal 2023 Forms 10-K.

| Company | Fiscal 2023 advertising expense/costs (US$ billions) | Filing evidence |
|---|---:|---|
| **Pfizer** | **Approximately 3.7** | Note 1.J states: “Advertising expenses totaled approximately $3.7 billion in 2023.” Printed p. 61 (PDF p. 70), *PFE_2023_10K.pdf*. |
| **Walmart** | **4.1** | Note 1, “Advertising Costs,” states: “Advertising costs were $4.1 billion … for fiscal 2023.” Printed/PDF p. 64, *WMT_2023_10K.pdf*. |

The other six filings—**NVIDIA, Apple, JPMorgan Chase, Berkshire Hathaway, ExxonMobil and Boeing**—do not state a qualifying company-wide fiscal 2023 advertising-expense or advertising-cost amount.

In particular:
- **JPMorgan Chase’s $4.591 billion is labeled “Marketing,”** so it does not count (printed p. 57; PDF p. 59).
- **Berkshire Hathaway discusses reductions in GEICO’s advertising costs**, not a company-wide total advertising-expense amount (printed pp. K-37–K-38; PDF pp. 39–40).

Non-disclosure here does not mean zero advertising expense.
